reviews.title: One star. Because apparently zero isn’t an option
reviews.text:
If you’re looking for a sleep app that occasionally notices you slept, you’ve found it.

On multiple occasions, I’ve slept for six hours only to wake up and discover that, according to the app, I slept for six minutes. Apparently I’m not sleeping at night; I’m briefly losing consciousness and then staring at the ceiling for the remaining 5 hours and 54 minutes. Who knew?

Other nights, the app simply decides not to record my sleep at all. Perhaps it was tired and needed the night off.

Technical support and customer service are equally impressive: they simply don’t exist. Emails disappear into the void and requests for help go unanswered. Perhaps everyone in customer service and technical support is sleeping. If so, I hope someone is accurately tracking it.

A sleep-tracking app that can’t reliably track sleep has one fairly obvious problem: it fails at the one thing it exists to do.

Save your money. If I want wildly inaccurate information about how long I slept, I can make up a number myself. And unlike this company, I’ll be available if I have questions.

My recommendation? Try ShutEye instead. It has the rather revolutionary feature of actually tracking your sleep. Apparently, that’s a competitive advantage now.

However, at least 30% of the time, it simply gives me a 0 for my sleep score, and doesn’t record any information about my sleep. 

There are serious stability issues here and I have seen no progress toward resolving this issue.

reviews.title: Where’s the graph man
reviews.text: I really liked this app and have been using it for a while now to track my sleep to help with my ADHD. The graph that came with the report was super helpful for me with that since I was mainly using it to see when I was in different stages how many times I was waking up, how long it took me to fall asleep. All really helpful stuff that had convinced me to start looking into purchasing the premium subscription. Now I’m glad I didn’t after the update that removed the graph. I waited for a bit to see if any of these reviews convinced the devs to bring the graph back, but nope. Glad I haven’t purchased anything yet, because I’ll be looking for a different sleep app now that doesn’t randomly remove their main features.

Maybe it works great in other ways, but the onboarding was a horrible experience (and asking me to sign up for the paid program twice before I can even explore…)

reviews.title: Issues with tracking
reviews.text: I enjoy the app and the fact you receive a score. But for some reason, the first 1-2 hours of my sleep constantly gets registered as “no signal”. This ruins my sleep score every night. Fix this so my time in bed/asleep is more accurate.

reviews.title: Doesn't work if you use another sound app simultaneously
reviews.text: Because it uses a sonar type of technology, it doesn't work if you use another sound app simultaneously, even using ear buds. Since using spoken-word apps (podcasts, books, certain apps) to fall asleep is the single best thing I've ever done to facilitate sleep onset, this for me was a deal breaker. It records as "paused" and "0 minutes sleep". It does have it's own peaceful, fall-asleep sounds, if you're OK using those, but you can't listen to your own choice of content thru any of your other apps.

reviews.title: Needs to allow ALL data from Apple Health…not just data from Apple Watch
reviews.text:
I have been using the  premium version of the app for a while and although I find the metrics unique and informative, there are areas in which it falls a bit short.
I use my Apple Watch to track my sleep and while AH is an overall good sleep data analyzer, it does not provide a “sleep score.” Personally, I like having an actual score, which is why I like using “sleep score”
My criticism of the app stems largely from the fact that while you can “add data” in AH, sleep score does not account for that added data.
For example, this morning, AH said I woke up at 4:28AM, which I did; briefly. 
However I didn’t get up fully out of bed for the day until 5:30. AH allows me to “add data” in the health app for that hour.
I feel as though sleep score should include that “added data” and not just the information from my Apple Watch exclusively.

Will keep the app; but not the premium version
